newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Comalco smelters shy away from growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Comalco smelters shy away from growth.

text.p: Aluminium producer Comalco Ltd said on Monday it was shelving growth plans in favour of improving operations in smelters in Australia and New Zealand.

As part of the shift, "some layoffs" among staff had occurred at the Bell Bay, Tasmania and Tiwai Point, New Zealand smelters, said a spokesman for the company, 67 percent owned by Anglo-Australian mining group RTZ-CRA.
The changes aim to improve the efficiencies of the smelter to counter ballooning operating costs, the spokesman said.
But the change were not expected to impair production at Comalco's three smelter sites, he added.

The situation for Comalco has been aggravated by a 16 percent fall in the average aluminmum prices in 1996 and unfavourable Australia-U.S. dollar exchange rates, which were weighing on the bottom line, the spokesman said.
"Every one U.S. cent move in the average aluminium price means A$9 million in net profit," he said.
Comalco is almost as sensitive to exchange rates, with each one cent representing A$7 million in profits, he added.

Analysts said the shift made sense after a period of growth at Comalco, although the market punished the aluminium maker on Monday, in response to a newpaper report that it may be mulling an exit from smelting altogether.
The company declined to comment on the report.

Comalco closed 16 cents down at A$6.70. A US$12 a tonne drop in the aluminium price on the London Metal Exchange on Friday despite a decline in LME warehouse stocks, usually a positive, probably attributed to the sell-off, analysts said.
"They've basically been in a growth mode for about three years and now the company recognises its time to focus on operations," said Macquarie Equities analyst Peter O'Connor.

Analysts estimate that Comalco has overall operating costs of around 55 US cents per pound of aluminium versus a current market price of around 70 cents, making it a higher cost producer than its domestic rivals.
Comalco in December warned of losses in the second half period to December 31, 1996 versus an after-tax operating profit of A$43.9 million in the preceding half year.
